title: 21 Sep 2026 (Riyadh)
des: Saudi Prometric paediatrics recall, Riyadh, 21 September 2026

questions.question: A child suddenly cannot stand after a URTI. He is alert, has only ataxia and CT is normal. What is the diagnosis?
A child has ataxia and loss of bladder and bowel control after an infection. What is the investigation?
A child with temperature 38 °C has been convulsing for 40 minutes. What is this?
questions.exp: Seizure ≥ 30 minutes (operationally ≥ 5 minutes) is status epilepticus; consider CNS infection.

questions.question: A febrile toddler has a 3-minute generalised tonic-clonic seizure and is normal on examination afterwards. What is the management?
questions.exp: Simple febrile seizures need no investigation beyond finding the fever source.

questions.question: A child has a focal seizure with upward eye deviation for 3 minutes then sleeps for 30 minutes. What is the next investigation?
questions.exp: A first afebrile focal seizure needs EEG, and usually MRI.

questions.question: A 4-month-old's head circumference grew from 35 cm at birth to 47 cm; feeding is unchanged. What is the investigation?
questions.exp: Fontanelle is open; ultrasound is first-line.

questions.question: A term baby's head circumference was 32 cm at birth and is 36 cm at 4 months. What is the next investigation?
questions.exp: Head growth of only 4 cm over 4 months indicates microcephaly; MRI looks for structural causes, plus TORCH and genetic tests.

questions.question: A toddler has typical breath-holding spells. What is the management?
A toddler has atypical spells of breath-holding with prolonged stiffening and jerking. Which investigation helps exclude epilepsy?
questions.exp: Atypical or frequent spells may need EEG and ECG (long QT).

questions.question: What is the typical length gain per month in months 3 to 6?
questions.exp: Growth velocity slows over the first year.

questions.question: A term newborn weighs 3 kg and is 50 cm long. What is the expected head circumference?
questions.exp: Normal term HC is about 35 cm.

questions.question: How is pain assessed in children?
questions.exp: FLACC, Wong-Baker faces or numerical scales depending on age.

questions.question: A 1-year-old with fever and a blanchable rash is irritable with GCS 13 and otherwise normal examination. What is next?
questions.exp: Irritability in an infant may be the only sign of meningitis. The recall said GCS 10, which would contraindicate LP.
questions.a: Lumbar puncture after blood culture, if no contraindication

questions.question: A child has fever and a non-blanching rash and looks ill. What is the first investigation before antibiotics?
questions.exp: Take a blood culture and give ceftriaxone immediately.

questions.question: A child with fever and purpura is suspected of meningococcaemia. What is the organism?
A 7-month-old arches, extends the arms and legs and grunts when the bottle is removed after feeds, then is normal. Examination is normal. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Sandifer posturing is linked to feeds and reflux.

questions.question: How are tics diagnosed?
An infant has clusters of flexor spasms with developmental regression. What is the diagnosis?
A girl falls from a horse, GCS 10, spine X-ray is normal but she cannot move her legs. What is next?
A 9-year-old has twice-monthly attacks of periumbilical pain lasting hours, with pallor, vomiting and photophobia, normal in between, and a family history of migraine. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Abdominal pain is the main symptom; normal between episodes.

questions.question: A child has recurrent stereotyped episodes of intense vomiting lasting days with complete wellness between them. What is the diagnosis?
What is the cause of a cephalhaematoma?
questions.exp: Limited by suture lines, unlike caput or subgaleal bleeds.

questions.question: A febrile infant with HR 160 and BP 60/40 has received two 20 mL/kg saline boluses and is still shocked. What is next?
questions.exp: After 40-60 mL/kg, fluid-refractory shock needs inotropes. The recall writer chose a third saline bolus.
questions.d: Start inotropes (adrenaline) while giving a further fluid bolus

questions.question: An infant falls down stairs, is conscious, then becomes drowsy an hour later. What is the diagnosis?
A child has a facial port-wine stain and intracranial calcification. What is the next step to support the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Sturge-Weber: leptomeningeal angioma, seizures and glaucoma.

questions.question: A child has recurrent infections, ataxia and very low IgA and IgG. Which test supports the diagnosis?
A child with Gottron papules and proximal weakness is evaluated. Which test is most useful?
A child has lower limb hypotonia and hyporeflexia with extensor plantars. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Upper motor neuron sign with acute flaccidity suggests spinal shock.

questions.question: In transverse myelitis, what does MRI show?
questions.d: T2 hyperintensity with gadolinium enhancement of the cord

questions.question: A 3-year-old with otitis media on amoxicillin for 5 days becomes irritable and convulses. What is next?
A 5-year-old has drug-resistant seizures and white skin patches. What is the diagnosis?
A 2-year-old's mother cannot understand his speech, and he responds only when she uses gestures with speech. What is the next step?
questions.exp: Responding only to visual cues suggests hearing loss; audiology first. The recall writer chose closed questions.

questions.question: A neonate with Rh disease had an exchange transfusion via a UVC and now has haematuria and a flank mass. What is the investigation?
A 7-year-old has facial, scrotal and leg oedema, BP 95/55, albumin 27 g/L and high triglycerides. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: Prednisolone 60 mg/m²/day for minimal change disease.

questions.question: A 15-month-old cannot sit without support, has recurrent chest infections and tongue fasciculations. What is the investigation?
A boy has a long narrow face and large ears. What is the investigation?
A 3-year-old has a smooth flank mass that does not cross the midline, with haematuria. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Wilms rarely crosses the midline; neuroblastoma often does.

questions.question: A 2-year-old is ill with an irregular abdominal mass crossing the midline, periorbital bruising and raised urinary catecholamines. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Raccoon eyes from orbital metastasis; VMA and HVA raised.

questions.question: A newborn has a skin-covered occipital sac. What is the diagnosis?
A 32-week preterm has tachypnoea, retractions and cyanosis, with white lungs and air bronchograms on X-ray. What is the diagnosis?
A child has fever, a petechial rash starting on the wrists and ankles and spreading to the trunk, and severe abdominal pain after a tick bite. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Rickettsia rickettsii; treat with doxycycline at any age.

questions.question: A child has fever, a rash starting on the face then spreading, and posterior auricular and suboccipital lymphadenopathy. What is the diagnosis?
How is mumps confirmed?
questions.exp: Buccal swab PCR near Stensen's duct.
questions.a: Viral PCR from buccal (parotid duct) swab or IgM

questions.question: A newborn has vomiting, dehydration, sodium 127 and potassium 6.3. What is the diagnosis?
Which vaccine should not be given to household contacts of a child with ALL?
questions.exp: OPV virus is shed and may infect the immunocompromised; contacts can have MMR and varicella.

questions.question: A 5-year-old has nocturnal enuresis without daytime wetting. What is a likely mechanism?
questions.c: Nocturnal polyuria or reduced bladder capacity

questions.question: A 5-year-old has primary nocturnal enuresis without daytime symptoms. What is the management?
questions.exp: Common at 5 years; treat from 6-7 years if bothersome.

questions.question: What does hypercalcaemia cause?
questions.exp: Nephrogenic DI-like polyuria, constipation and lethargy.

questions.question: A 2-year-old has fever 39.3 °C, dark urine, abdominal tenderness, BP 125/85 and urine with WBC and RBC. What is the diagnosis?
A toilet-trained uncircumcised 3-year-old needs a urine sample. What is the best method?
A child has acute scrotal pain and swelling from epididymitis. What is the most likely organism?
questions.exp: Prepubertal epididymitis is usually from urinary pathogens; exclude torsion first.

questions.question: A boy has asymmetric testicular enlargement, high testosterone and low LH and FSH. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Peripheral precocious puberty with a unilateral testicular mass.

questions.question: A girl with constipation has recurrent febrile UTIs. Which investigation looks for renal scarring?
questions.exp: DMSA is done 4-6 months after infection.

questions.question: A child with phaeochromocytoma has BP 190/110. What is the first drug?
A child has polyuria, urine osmolality 155 that does not rise after desmopressin. What is the diagnosis?
A child with sickle cell disease had a transfusion 3 weeks ago and comes for hepatitis A vaccine. What should be done?
questions.exp: Inactivated vaccines are not affected by blood products; live vaccines (MMR, varicella) are delayed.

questions.question: A child with iron deficiency starts oral iron. What responds first?
A child with Hodgkin lymphoma has cervical, mediastinal and para-aortic node involvement and no B symptoms. What is the stage?
questions.exp: Nodes on both sides of the diaphragm = III; no B symptoms = A.

questions.question: A boy has thrombocytopenia with small platelets, eczema and recurrent infections. What is the diagnosis?
A child has gum bleeding, and the mother and sister have menorrhagia. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Autosomal dominant mucocutaneous bleeding. The recall writer said a platelet function defect.

questions.question: A newborn with Down syndrome has WBC 10, platelets 30 and 60% blasts. What is the management?
questions.exp: TAM usually resolves by 3 months; 20-30% later develop AML.

questions.question: A child has petechiae and very low platelets after a URTI. What is the diagnosis?
A newborn after meconium-stained delivery is apnoeic, floppy and cyanosed. What is the first step after initial steps?
questions.exp: Routine tracheal suction is no longer recommended; start PPV within 1 minute.
questions.b: Positive-pressure ventilation for 30 seconds then reassess heart rate

questions.question: Why are children with sickle cell disease prone to infection with encapsulated bacteria?
questions.exp: Autosplenectomy and defective alternative complement pathway.
questions.a: Functional asplenia with reduced opsonisation (low properdin)

questions.question: A child with recurrent allergies has swollen lips, wheeze and hypotension after a food. What is the treatment?
A hypotensive child has warm skin, capillary refill 1 second and bounding pulses. What type of shock is this?
What is a common complication of tetralogy of Fallot?
questions.exp: Complications include hypercyanotic spells, polycythaemia, stroke, brain abscess and endocarditis.
questions.a: Cerebral thrombosis or abscess from polycythaemia

questions.question: A 10-month-old has cyanosis, oligaemic lungs and right ventricular hypertrophy. What is the diagnosis?
A child has distended neck veins and muffled heart sounds with hypotension. What type of shock is this?
questions.exp: Tamponade and tension pneumothorax cause obstructive shock.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of infective endocarditis in children?
questions.exp: Staph aureus is now as common in some series, especially with lines. The recall writer chose Staph aureus.
questions.c: Viridans streptococci (with Staph aureus close behind)

questions.question: A child has peaked T waves and paraesthesia. What is the first treatment?
A child took a large dose of decongestant and has SVT. What is the treatment if stable?
A short child (height 115 cm) has an ejection systolic murmur at the right upper sternal border. What is the lesion?
What is the appropriate age for closure of a large VSD with pulmonary hypertension?
questions.exp: Repair before irreversible pulmonary vascular disease. The recall writer chose 6-12 months.

questions.question: A 4-year-old has day and night wetting with urgency. What is the most likely cause?
How much sodium is in 0.45% saline?
A child who had an atrial switch operation for TGA has bradycardia. What does the ECG show?
questions.exp: Atrial baffles damage the sinus node.

questions.question: Which is a major Duke criterion for infective endocarditis?
questions.exp: Major: echo evidence and typical organisms in blood cultures.

questions.question: A child has upslanting eyes and a single palmar crease. What is the most common cardiac lesion?
A child has fever, tachycardia, muffled heart sounds and a pericardial rub after a URTI. What is the diagnosis?
A ventilated child after head trauma has GCS 5, hypertension and cerebral oedema on CT. What is given to reduce ICP?
questions.exp: Hypertonic saline or mannitol; steroids are not used in TBI.

questions.question: In a child with severe head injury, which finding predicts poor outcome?
A boy with haemophilia A has a haemarthrosis, FVIII 0.1% and a low-titre inhibitor of 2 BU. What is the treatment?
A child has short stature and a high-pitched voice with low growth hormone. What is the treatment?
A 7-week-old with suspected pyloric stenosis has sunken eyes, dry mouth and a sunken fontanelle. Which fluid is used?
questions.exp: Correct dehydration and hypochloraemic alkalosis before pyloromyotomy.

questions.question: A term baby born after polyhydramnios has bilious vomiting on day 2 and a double-bubble sign. What is the diagnosis?
A child has retching without vomiting, an NG tube cannot be passed, and he is unstable. What is the management?
A pale child has maroon stools. What is the investigation?
A 12-year-old girl has bloody diarrhoea, growth failure, raised platelets and ESR. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Growth failure is typical of Crohn.

questions.question: A child has recurrent chest infections and sweat chloride 68 mmol/L. What is the diagnosis?
A neonate has bilious vomiting and a corkscrew duodenum on contrast. What is the diagnosis?
A child with coeliac disease has itchy grouped vesicles on the elbows. What is the rash?
questions.exp: IgA deposits; responds to gluten-free diet and dapsone.

questions.question: What is the most commonly ingested foreign body in children?
A coin in the oesophagus moved after the mother gave water. What is next?
questions.exp: Coins that pass into the stomach can be observed. The recall writer chose fluoroscopy with magnet.
questions.b: Repeat X-ray; endoscopic removal if still in the oesophagus

questions.question: A 6-year-old eating peanuts suddenly coughs and gags, cannot speak and has severe retractions. What is the first step?
questions.exp: Conscious child with ineffective cough: abdominal thrusts.

questions.question: A 6-year-old who cannot speak after choking on a peanut has severe retractions. Where is the foreign body?
questions.exp: Aphonia and severe distress suggest upper airway obstruction.

questions.question: A child has painless rectal bleeding and multiple hamartomatous colonic polyps. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Juvenile polyps are hamartomatous; more than 5 suggests the syndrome (SMAD4/BMPR1A).

questions.question: Which condition is an indication for parenteral nutrition?
questions.exp: TPN when the gut cannot absorb enough nutrition.

questions.question: A child with ALL has multiple small liver and spleen lesions on ultrasound. What is the cause?
A 2-week-old has jaundice with high serum bile acids and normal blood count. What is the most important question?
questions.exp: Pale stools suggest biliary atresia; urgent conjugated bilirubin.

questions.question: What acid-base disturbance is associated with cystic fibrosis?
A child with abdominal distension has multiple air-fluid levels on X-ray. What prompts surgical referral?
questions.exp: Obstruction on imaging with bilious vomiting.

questions.question: A 4-year-old stutters. What is the advice?
A teenage girl has hallucinations and disorganised speech, with a family history. What is the diagnosis?
A child argues with adults, blames others and is often angry, without aggression to people or property. What is the diagnosis?
A child is aggressive, steals from classmates and has hit his mother. What is the diagnosis?
A 6-year-old has stolen money. What is the advice?
questions.d: Make him return it and discuss why

questions.question: A 4.5-year-old sucks his thumb. What is the advice?
Parents are worried about their child's short stature. What is the most important information?
A girl had menarche at 10.5 years and now at 13 her growth has slowed markedly. What is the cause?
questions.b: Early puberty with growth plate fusion

questions.question: A boy has intellectual disability, cataracts, rickets and renal tubular dysfunction; his maternal uncle and grandfather are affected. What is the diagnosis?
An infant with RSV bronchiolitis becomes hypoactive with higher fever. What is the cause?
questions.exp: Secondary bacterial infection is suspected when fever rises late.

questions.question: A child has fever, sore throat, a sandpaper rash and a strawberry tongue. What is the organism?
A child has fever, diarrhoea and a vesicular rash on the feet and mouth. What is the management?
questions.exp: HFMD is self-limiting. The recall writer chose acyclovir.

questions.question: A child with bloody diarrhoea, dehydration and oliguria is assessed. Which test distinguishes pre-renal from intrinsic renal failure?
Which nutrient is higher in cow's milk than breast milk?
questions.exp: Cow's milk has 3 times more protein and more sodium.

questions.question: A child with cystic fibrosis has a chest infection resistant to antibiotics. What is the likely organism?
A child with diabetes has white plaques on the tongue that scrape off. What is the diagnosis?
What must be included in research consent?
questions.exp: Purpose, risks, benefits, voluntariness and the right to withdraw.
questions.a: Aim of the study and the right to withdraw at any time

questions.question: What does completing 3 doses of hepatitis B vaccine reduce?
questions.exp: HBV vaccine is the first anti-cancer vaccine.

questions.question: A newborn's mother has HIV. What is given to the baby?
A child with ALL in neutropenia has pyoderma. What is the empirical treatment?
What is the IV treatment of pyelonephritis in a young infant?
questions.exp: Nitrofurantoin does not reach renal tissue.
questions.a: Ampicillin plus gentamicin (or a third-generation cephalosporin)

questions.question: A child with atopy has sudden night-time barking cough without fever. What is the diagnosis?
A toxic child has fever, drooling and stridor. What is the diagnosis?
An asthmatic child finished 5 days of oral steroids and is on inhaled steroids. He is due his 4-year vaccines. What should be done?
questions.exp: Short courses or < 2 mg/kg prednisolone do not contraindicate live vaccines.

questions.question: What is an indication for mechanical ventilation in acute asthma?
A mother is worried about her asthmatic child in winter. What advice is given?
A child grinds his teeth at night, affecting the jaw. What is the management?
questions.exp: Splints protect teeth when there is wear or TMJ pain.
questions.b: Dental referral for an occlusal splint

questions.question: An asthmatic child presents with cyanosis, hyper-resonance and reduced air entry on the left. What is the immediate treatment?
A 7-month-old has vomiting, irritability and jaundice after starting fruit purée. Which enzyme is deficient?
A mother wants to withdraw ventilation from her newborn with multiple anomalies, who will die if extubated. What should the doctor do?
questions.exp: In Saudi practice, DNR and withdrawal decisions require agreement of at least two (often three) consultants.
questions.d: Explain that the decision needs agreement of two consultants and an ethics review

questions.question: A junior diagnoses UTI but the senior stops treatment before it is given. What is this?
A senior teaches a junior about keeping promises and commitment to patients. Which principle is this?
What is the most common type of error in hospitals?
A child is abused by his father. What should the doctor do?
questions.d: Refer to social services and the protection authority

questions.question: A child is stung by a scorpion. What is the most useful investigation?
questions.exp: Look for myocarditis and hyperglycaemia. The recall writer chose CBC.
questions.c: ECG with glucose and electrolytes (and CBC)

questions.question: A child with glycogen storage disease has hypoglycaemia, high lactate, hepatomegaly and doll-like face. What is the management of acute hypoglycaemia?
questions.exp: Glucagon does not work in GSD I; frequent feeds and cornstarch long-term.
questions.d: Continuous glucose infusion (or continuous NG feeds)

questions.question: A child was in a house fire. What is the most important level to measure?
questions.exp: Pulse oximetry is falsely normal in CO poisoning; also consider cyanide.

questions.question: A 6-year-old has right upper lobe consolidation and crackles on the left. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: Bilateral findings at school age suggest atypical pneumonia; amoxicillin for typical lobar. Details limited.

questions.question: A child with pneumonia on ceftriaxone worsens with a large pleural effusion. What is next?
A child has epistaxis with no bleeding disorder or trauma. What is the first step?
questions.exp: Little's area bleeding stops with pressure.
questions.c: Compress the soft nose with the head tilted forward for 10 minutes

questions.question: A child has allergic rhinitis. What is the first-line treatment?
What is a common cause of epistaxis in children with allergic rhinitis?
A child has periodic limb movements affecting sleep. What is the investigation?
questions.exp: PSG quantifies limb movements; check ferritin.

questions.question: A child has fever and a brassy cough with no drooling, worsening despite croup treatment. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Staph aureus; needs airway and antibiotics.

questions.question: A febrile child is playful with no meningism, a clear chest and a high WBC; a blood culture is taken. Which organism is most likely?
A child runs, knows his first name but not his full name, climbs stairs without alternating feet and uses 3-word sentences. What is the age?
questions.exp: Two to three word phrases and stairs two feet per step at 2 years. The recall writer chose 2.5 but thought 2 was right.

questions.question: A child has respiratory distress with bronchial breathing, a lower zone opacity, abdominal pain and a palpable liver. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Lower-lobe pneumonia causes abdominal pain; hyperinflation pushes the liver down.

questions.question: What reactivates acetylcholinesterase in organophosphate poisoning?
questions.exp: Atropine treats muscarinic effects; pralidoxime reactivates the enzyme.

questions.question: A child develops extrapyramidal symptoms after an antiemetic. What is the treatment?
What are airborne precautions?
questions.d: N95 respirator with hand hygiene and negative-pressure room

questions.question: What should be worn for contact precautions for MRSA?
What should a discharge plan include?
How should a morphine dose of half a milligram be written?
questions.exp: Always use a leading zero and never a trailing zero.

questions.question: A child has a nasal "polyp" since birth. What is the investigation?
questions.exp: Congenital midline nasal masses may connect intracranially.

questions.question: A child has a nasal dermoid cyst with a sinus above the nose. What is a complication?
questions.exp: Imaging before excision because of possible intracranial tract.
